review_candidates.title: Customer Operations
review_candidates.description: Company Overview At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future. Department Overview Silvus is seeking a Customer Operations Manager who will report to the International Customer Operations Lead. The successful individual in this role will serve as the primary post-sales operational liaison between our key customers and Silvus manufacturing organization and internal associated departments. The mission is to manage purchase orders, production schedules, delivery coordination to ensure components are delivered on time and integrated successfully into the customer’s long-term production roadmap. This position is eligible for 100% remote work depending on location. The following is a list of at least some of the current essential job functions of the position. Management may assign or reassign duties and responsibilities at any time at its discretion Job Description Key Responsibilities Customer Relationship Management: Serve as the primary point of contact for customer post sale, managing day-to-day operational needs and escalations. Lead Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) to report on delivery performance, quality metrics, and roadmap alignment. Demand Planning & Forecast Integration: Work directly with customer demand planners to ingest production forecasts. Translate these into actionable data for our internal manufacturing and supply chain teams to prevent stockouts or overages. Delivery Management: Track and manage open purchase orders to ensure on-time delivery commitments are met, partnering with manufacturing and logistics to resolve delays. Technical Advocacy & Issue Resolution: Identify technical hurdles or integration challenges the customer is facing. Partner with Engineering to resolve issues and manage the formal escalation process for any hardware defects or shipping delays. Lifecycle Management: Monitor component performance in the field. Manage the communication of End-of-Life (EOL) notices and transition customers to next-generation components. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Act as the "Voice of the Customer" internally, providing feedback to Product Development to influence the design of future components or products. RMA Management: Managing the Return Merchandise Authorization process - making sure that if a part fails, the customer gets a replacement immediately and your engineering team gets the "dead" part back for analysis. Regional Expertise: Navigate the specific logistical, legal, and contractual complexities unique to key countries like Germany and the Ukrainian theater. Perform other related duties of which the above are representative. Basic Requirements A self-motivated professional who thrives in fast-paced, ambiguous environments and takes full ownership of multitasking and shifting priorities. Languages: Excellent verbal, written, and presentation skills in English and either German or Ukrainian. Education: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, or a related technical field. review_candidates.title: Controller (International, Remote)
review_candidates.description: About the role The company. A fractional finance and accounting firm that acts as the finance department for fast-growing US healthcare and technology companies. Clients run several entities and sites, so accuracy, speed and clear communication matter as much as technical skill. The role. You are the senior accounting owner across the client portfolio. You run each month-end close, review the accounting team's work, and sign off on financial statements before they reach client leadership. You also build the controls and checklists that take the founders out of day-to-day review. Location and hours. Fully remote. You must overlap with US Pacific Time at least 4 hours every working day (about 7:00–11:00 am PT), with more overlap during the first week of each month. Reporting line. Reports to a company founder and works closely with the reporting and forecasting lead. What you will do Own the month-end close Run the close on a 7-business-day target with a 5-day expense cutoff, using a close calendar and checklist you maintain. Review bank, credit card and balance sheet reconciliations. Sign off on accruals, prepaids, fixed assets, and payroll and benefits liabilities. Review recurring and manual journal entries before posting, including payroll, benefits, PEO, accrued payroll and PTO, lease and revenue entries. Reconcile intercompany balances so each entity's receivable matches the related entity's payable. Prepare or review the close workbook: consolidated P&L and balance sheet, trended balance sheet commentary, and month-over-month and vendor variance analysis. Technical accounting Apply US GAAP, including ASC 842 leases (schedules, straight-line expense, CAM) and ASC 606 revenue recognition for contract and per-member-per-month revenue. Resolve questions from clients, auditors and tax preparers, and document the positions taken. Clean up legacy balances: stale accrued revenue, credit memos, duplicate or uncleared bill payments, and negative liabilities. Review and coach the team Review the daily output of staff accountants and bookkeepers in other time zones, with written feedback that is specific and kind. Keep review workbooks current so every open item has an owner and a status. Set coding standards by department, location and class, and keep the chart of accounts consistent across entities. Reporting and controls Deliver monthly financial packages to client leadership on schedule and join client finance reviews when needed. Support the weekly cash flow forecast and forecast-to-actual variance commentary. Document and improve controls: expense and card policy, receipts, approval workflows, vendor payments (Bill.com, Brex) and segregation of duties. Find where AI and automation can remove manual close steps, and run the pilots. What we are looking for Required 7+ years of accounting experience, including 3+ years as a Controller, Assistant Controller or Senior Accounting Manager. Strong US GAAP knowledge. CPA or an equivalent (ACCA, CA) preferred. Hands-on multi-entity closes in QuickBooks Online, and comfort with Bill.com, Brex or a similar spend platform and a payroll system such as Rippling. Experience reviewing payroll journal entries, benefits and PEO accounting, and accrued payroll and PTO. Advanced Google Sheets or Excel: pivots, lookups, reconciliations and variance analysis. Excellent written English and the ability to explain a variance to a non-accountant. Reliable internet, a quiet workspace, and a schedule that meets the Pacific Time overlap. Strongly preferred Experience with healthcare or technology companies. Experience in an outsourced, fractional or agency accounting firm serving several clients. Familiarity with Fathom, Coefficient or similar reporting tools, and with AI tools in accounting workflows. Experience with multi-location (site-level) profitability reporting. How we will measure success Each client's close finishes on the published calendar, with a 7-business-day target. Fewer than 5 transaction errors per review cycle across the team. Reconciliations and review workbooks have no unexplained items at sign-off. The founders are no longer the first line of review.
